source.title: Widespread long-range cis coordination and promoter competition shape nascent transcription

targets.question: When does cis nascent coordination exceed matched trans coordination, and how does it depend on distance and expression?
requirements: Two matched alleles in each simulated cell for cis/trans
Matched localization/detection model and sample counts

targets.question: Can active-promoter competition reduce cis correlation relative to a matched trans control?
targets.implementation: Four-promoter stochastic reference with shared cell-level variability, mutual cis inhibition, RNA production/removal and imperfect detection. Qualitative sufficiency test; not the unpublished supporting-parameter scan.

targets.question: Which mechanisms alter nascent coordination and local molecular co-fluctuations under distance and expression controls?
targets.implementation: Spatial-model ablations of TF/recruitment, nucleosomes, marks, cohesin, body responses and chromatin mechanics. A single chain does not supply matched trans alleles.

targets.question: Do expression, genome organization and molecular-state modules discriminate cis-enhanced and cis-reduced pairs?
targets.status: Not reproduced. Requires the cell-level dataset, observation model, analysis choices and independent validation. SIF associations are not imposed as causal facts.

important_distinctions: Nascent-positive is not identical to promoter ON or mature RNA count.
A finite minimum sampled distance does not prove that historical contacts never occurred.
Detection efficiency attenuates correlations depending on marginal probabilities; no universal correction factor is assumed.
Prescribed body response multipliers are model hypotheses, not conversions of SIF fluorescence to kinetic rates.
20 Mb at 200 bp requires 100000 beads, beyond the current supported implementation.
